title: The global operator is an endomorphism of a perfect complex
statement:
Fix the coefficient
conventions, let $c=(c_1,c_2):C\to X\times_sX$ be an
admissible cohomological
correspondence whose ordinary leg $c_2$ is
proper, and let
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ with correspondence
$u:Lc_2^*K\to Rc_1^!K$. Then the global operator $T_c(u)$ of
[def-trf-global-operator] is a morphism of
$D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$ in the sense of
[def-trf-categorical-trace]: every intermediate complex of the
composite defining $T_c(u)$ is compact-support cohomology of a
finite-Tor constructible
complex.

proof.text: The coefficient conventions fix $A=A_{E,n}$ with $n\geq1$ and $\ell\ne p$. By [def-trf-correspondence], $X,C$ are separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $c_1$ is exceptionally admissible at $A$; the domain of [def-trf-admissibility] makes $c_1$ separated finite type. Properness of $c_2$ makes it separated finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Thus the hypotheses of the finite-Tor stability theorem are available for both legs. The source and target in [def-trf-global-operator] are $R\Gamma_c(X,K)$. Since $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, [prop-trf-compact-support-perfectness] makes this complex perfect in the sense of [def-trf-categorical-trace].

Put $H=Lc_2^*K$. Clause (i) of [thm-sf-ctf-stability] gives $H\in D^b_{ctf}(C,A)$, and clause (iii), applied to $c_2$ and $H$, gives $Rc_{2*}H\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$. This is finite-Tor constructibility as defined in [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], not merely bounded constructibility. Apply [prop-trf-compact-support-perfectness] on $C$ to $H$ and on $X$ to $Rc_{2*}H$. It follows that both ordinary-leg intermediate complexes $R\Gamma_c(C,H)$ and $R\Gamma_c(X,Rc_{2*}H)$ are perfect.

Put $J=Rc_1^!K$ for the specified constructible exceptional functor of [def-trf-admissibility]. Clause (v) of [thm-sf-ctf-stability] gives $J\in D^b_{ctf}(C,A)$, and clause (iv), applied to $c_1$ and $J$, gives $Rc_{1!}J\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$. Apply [prop-trf-compact-support-perfectness] on $C$ to $J$ and on $X$ to $Rc_{1!}J$. Thus both exceptional-leg intermediate complexes $R\Gamma_c(C,J)$ and $R\Gamma_c(X,Rc_{1!}J)$ are perfect. No unrestricted ambient right adjoint is used.

The compact-support functors are those of [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. In [def-trf-global-operator], the first identification is $R\Gamma_c(X,Rc_{2*}H)\simeq R\Gamma_c(X,Rc_{2!}H)\simeq R\Gamma_c(C,H)$, using proper coincidence and compact-support composition for $a_X\circ c_2=a_C$. The second is the inverse of $R\Gamma_c(X,Rc_{1!}J)\simeq R\Gamma_c(C,J)$, using composition for $a_X\circ c_1=a_C$. That definition already specifies these identifications, the ordinary unit, the arrow induced by $u$, and the exceptional counit as a composite in $D(A)$. Steps 1–3 show that every displayed object is compact-support cohomology of a finite-Tor constructible complex and is perfect. By [def-trf-categorical-trace], $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)=\operatorname{Perf}(A)$ is a full subcategory of $D(A)$: its Hom sets between these objects are the ambient Hom sets. Each of the five arrows therefore belongs to this full subcategory, and composition there is ambient composition. Their composite is the same $T_c(u)$, hence the asserted endomorphism of a perfect complex.

split_report.summary: Audited the earlier attempt against the current blueprint and every cited statement. Divided the proof into hypothesis and endpoint checks, ordinary-leg intermediate perfectness, exceptional-leg intermediate perfectness, and the elementary full-subcategory argument for the existing operator. Retained the repair from strong ambient admissibility to constructible stability. Corrected duplicated Mathlib directory prefixes and reran all four search kinds, with a second semantic phrasing and a whole-Mathlib grep. No new nodes; statement unchanged.
split_report.blueprint: Steps 1–4 realize the current blueprint proof paragraph: endpoint perfectness; the two ordinary-leg objects; the two exceptional-leg objects; the proper/composition comparisons and full-subcategory conclusion.

tool_uses.why: The global-operator unit supplies the composite and its four stages but no preservation theorem; this six-functor stability result is used as a generic black box for finite-Tor constructibility under pullback, direct images, compact-support direct image, and exceptional inverse image.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q90-5da15bfa2 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item and every cited statement. The statement matches main-20261015 and the master copy word for word: n>=1, ell!=p, admissible correspondence, c_2 proper, K in D^b_ctf, and every intermediate complex perfect, in Perf(A)=D^b_fin(A), a full subcategory of D(A) by def-trf-categorical-trace. Step 1: correspondence, admissibility and the proper-morphism definition make X, C, c_1 and c_2 separated finite type. prop-trf-compact-support-perfectness gives the endpoints. Its D^b_fin means perfect: I checked this against the sk-prop-sf-trace-perfectness unit text and the node's own proof, which concludes with a bounded complex of finite free modules. Step 2: thm-sf-ctf-stability (i) and (iii) put Lc_2^*K in D^b_ctf(C) and Rc_2*Lc_2^*K in D^b_ctf(X); perfectness then gives both ordinary-leg objects. Step 3: stability (v) and (iv) apply to the specified constructible Rc_1^! of def-trf-admissibility. The blueprint's citation of strong ambient admissibility item (3) is stale, since def-trf-admissibility now excludes that notion with an elliptic-curve counterexample. Replacing it with constructible stability is correct and does not weaken the target. Step 4 (elementary): the directions of alpha_{c_2} and gamma_{c_1}^{-1} match def-trf-global-operator, and the full-subcategory argument is valid. There are no new nodes, no duplicates and no cycle. I accept the declared tool use of thm-sf-ctf-stability: the sk-d-operator route through sk-d-six only specifies constructible finiteness in a package and proves no preservation theorem. prop-trf-compact-support-perfectness is the blueprint proof's own citation, which the route check only records. Edge cases: the identity correspondence gives RΓ_c(A^1,A)=A(-1)[-2], which is perfect; for the Frobenius correspondence c_2=F is finite, hence proper; C empty or K=0 makes everything zero. Over Z/ℓ² the complex i_*(Z/ℓ) on a point shows the ctf hypothesis is needed. No fixes.
